# MapControlsGroup

The stacked zoom, compass, and locate affordances that sit over a map.

- **Import:** `import { MapControlsGroup } from "@kozmos-ds/react";`
- **Group:** SDK
- **Platforms:** React, SwiftUI and Compose; linked to its Figma component through Code Connect.
- **Storybook:** <https://vodoco.github.io/kozmos-design-system/storybook/?path=/docs/map-mapcontrolsgroup--docs>

## Example

From its `Default` story.

```tsx
import { MapControlsGroup, ThemeProvider } from "@kozmos-ds/react";

export function MapControlsGroupExample() {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider defaultTheme="light">
      <MapControlsGroup
        compassBearing={32}
        onZoomIn={() => console.log("zoom in")}
        onZoomOut={() => console.log("zoom out")}
        onCompassReset={() => console.log("reset bearing")}
        onMyLocation={() => console.log("locate me")}
      />
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

## MapControlsGroup

It forwards its ref to `HTMLDivElement`. Its props are `MapControlsGroupProps`, which extends `React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>`.

- `onZoomIn`: `() => void`, optional.
- `onZoomOut`: `() => void`, optional.
- `onCompassReset`: `() => void`, optional.
- `onMyLocation`: `() => void`, optional.
- `compassBearing`: `number`, optional, default `0`.
- `label`: `string`, optional, default `"Map controls"`.
- `zoomInLabel`: `string`, optional, default `"Zoom in"`.

  What each control is called, for a visitor who cannot see it.

  Hard-coded English until row 67: a German or Japanese device announced
  "Zoom in" whatever else the product had translated. The defaults stay
  English because a design system has no locale of its own — the product
  has one, and now has somewhere to put it.

- `zoomOutLabel`: `string`, optional, default `"Zoom out"`.
- `compassResetLabel`: `string`, optional, default `"Reset bearing"`.
- `locationState`: `UserLocationState`, optional, default `"off"`.
- `locationLabel`: `string`, optional, default `"Focus location"`.
- `locationStateLabel`: `string`, optional.

  The state the control shows under its name: "Off", "On". The SDK reads
  heading "On", as it reads following (decision 40). With no position
  (`unavailable`, `permission-denied`) the control draws this alone, on one
  line — the SDK's "No Location" — and its name still starts the accessible
  name.

- `locationHeadingDescription`: `string`, optional, default `"map turns with you"`.

  What heading adds to the name, for a screen reader: heading shows "On"
  as following does, and only its mark tells the two apart on screen.
  Read after the words the control shows. Default "map turns with you";
  the product translates it.

- `locationHeadingPausedDescription`: `string`, optional, default `"press to turn the map with you again"`.

  What a paused heading adds to the name, for a screen reader: with
  `heading-paused` the control shows "Off", as off does, and the next press
  brings the turning map back (decision 45). Read after the words the
  control shows. Default "press to turn the map with you again"; the product
  translates it.

- `locationPresentation`: `"icon-only" | "labelled"`, optional, default `"icon-only"`.
- `locationIcons`: `Partial<Record<UserLocationState, React.ReactNode>>`, optional.

  The mark for any location state, in place of the group's own.

  The group draws one per state (row 77), from the revamp. A product with
  its own artwork for a state passes that state alone; the others keep the
  group's marks. It is drawn in the control's colour, so artwork that uses
  `currentColor` follows the pressed tint as the group's own marks do.

- `locationRevealOnChange`: `boolean`, optional, default `false`.

  Let the location control widen to say its new mode whenever it changes,
  then collapse — `MapControlButton`'s `revealOnChange`. While it is set,
  `locationPresentation` is ignored.

  This and `locationLabelPlacement` are how the SDK's location control
  reads: icon-only over the map, "Focus / On" for a moment when the mode
  changes. Both are off by default, so a product that already relies on a
  fixed presentation sees nothing move.

  The step-free control, which takes this place during a route, follows
  the same three settings, so the corner reads the same either way.

- `locationLabelPlacement`: `"inline" | "stacked"`, optional, default `"inline"`.

  `stacked` sets the state under the name — `MapControlButton`'s `labelPlacement`.

- `onStepFreeChange`: `(stepFree: boolean) => void`, optional.

  While a route is active, a step-free control takes the location
  control's place: passing this draws it, and the location control is not
  drawn. Called with the setting the visitor asked for.

  The same button, in the same place, during wayfinding (Olcay,
  2026-09-27). Pass it only while the route is shown; leaving it out brings
  the location control back.

- `stepFree`: `boolean`, optional, default `false`.

  Whether the route is step-free now. Set it once the route it describes is
  the one on the map — a control that says "On" over a route with stairs is
  worse than one that is a moment late.

- `stepFreeLabel`: `string`, optional, default `"Step-free"`.

  The control's name. Default "Step-free"; the product translates it.

- `stepFreeOnLabel`: `string`, optional, default `"On"`.

  The state appended to the name while on. Default "On".

- `stepFreeOffLabel`: `string`, optional, default `"Off"`.

  The state appended to the name while off. Default "Off".

- `stepFreeIcon`: `React.ReactNode`, optional.

  The mark, in place of the wheelchair symbol `RouteOptionCard` uses for step-free.

- `children`: `ReactNode`, optional.

It also takes the attributes React's DOM types give it (`className`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, the event handlers among them).

## Types these props take

### UserLocationState

From `@kozmos-ds/product-contracts`.

```ts
/**
 * What the map is doing with the visitor's position, as the location control
 * shows it.
 *
 * `following` keeps the visitor centred; `heading` also turns the map with
 * them. `heading-paused` is heading remembered while the map has been moved
 * away from them (decision 45): the SDK's rotational Off, "Focus / Off" beside
 * the upright pointer in outline. The next press goes straight back to
 * `heading`, which is the product's to do.
 */
type UserLocationState =
  | "off"
  | "locating"
  | "following"
  | "heading"
  | "heading-paused"
  | "permission-denied"
  | "stale"
  | "unavailable";
```
